class.name: PlayerVirtualJoystick
class.brief_description: On-screen thumbstick that drives one player's own [PlayerInput].
class.description: A pawn reads it through its [InputComponent] like any other action, and never has to know whether the machine has a touchscreen. [b]Godot ships its own [VirtualJoystick], and for a single-player game that one is the better choice[/b] - it is themed, and a [PlayerInput] in passthrough forwards to [Input] anyway. This class exists for the two things the engine's cannot do. The first is ownership. The engine's stick writes to the global [Input] singleton, which merges every device, so with two people on one machine it moves both pawns. This one writes to the [PlayerInput] of the [LocalPlayer] at [member player_index] - which is the whole reason [PlayerInput] exists. The second is [member press_action]: an action held for as long as a finger is on the stick. That lets one gesture mean both "move" and "hold", which four axes alone cannot express. [codeblock] # Drag to fly, and the tether is live for as long as the finger is down. $Joystick.action_left = &"move_left" $Joystick.action_right = &"move_right" $Joystick.action_up = &"move_up" $Joystick.action_down = &"move_down" $Joystick.press_action = &"grab" [/codeblock] Touches are tracked by finger index in [code]_input[/code] rather than through GUI routing, because GUI routing hands a second finger to the same [Control] and one of the two is lost. Events are never marked handled, so buttons above keep working - the stick ignores anything outside its own rect, which is also how a HUD strip is kept clear: give the stick a rect that does not cover it. Hiding the node releases everything it holds, so a stick hidden mid-drag cannot leave a pawn flying.

method.name: get_value
method.description: The current stick offset, at most one unit long. Reading the actions through an [InputComponent] is usually better - this is for the rare caller that wants the raw stick rather than the actions it drives.

method.name: is_active
method.description: Whether a finger is currently on the stick.

method.name: reset
method.description: Drops the finger and releases every action the stick is holding. Call it when gameplay input is taken away - a pause, a cutscene, a menu - or the actions stay pressed through it. Hiding the node does this for you.

members.member: The action pressed with a strength proportional to how far the stick is pushed down. Same for the other three axes. Leave one empty to ignore that direction.
How far the stick must move, as a fraction of [member max_distance], before it reports anything at all.
Draws a plain ring and knob while a finger is down. Turn it off to draw the stick yourself, or to show nothing at all.
How far from its centre the stick can be pushed, in pixels. Full deflection at this distance.
Whether the stick appears under the finger or sits at the centre of this control.
Which [LocalPlayer] this stick belongs to. With no local player yet, it writes to the global [Input] singleton instead - the same fallback [InputComponent] makes.
An action held for as long as a finger is on the stick. Leave it empty for a stick that only moves.
Drags the centre along behind the finger once it passes [member max_distance]. Without it a long swipe pins the stick and the player loses the sense of which way is which.

signal.name: drag_ended
signal.description: The finger lifted, or the stick was reset or hidden.

signal.name: drag_started
signal.description: A finger landed on the stick.

constants.constant: The stick appears wherever the finger lands. This is the one-thumb layout: no fixed corner to reach for, so it works one-handed.
The stick sits at the centre of this control and stays there.
